population.note: FICTIONAL. One-line cycling arithmetic: ever 31.5% − current 20.7% = 10.8% of adults used and are off now; ≈10.0 pts of current users are on a second or later course and ≈3.6 pts of the off-now group restarted at least once before stopping again, so (10.0+3.6)/31.5 = 43% cycled. This fits one-year persistence of ~40% (≈48% in gated plans, up from 35/45% because $39–69 generics remove the price reason to stop) and ~45% restart within a year. Of ~271M adults: ≈56.1M current, ≈29.3M used and off now, ≈186M never used. Ever-use rose 7.5 pts (24.0→31.5), within the +9.1 ceiling; first-course starters from this window are ≈5.5 pts of current users, and the rest of the +6.1 rise is restarts. Age check: 18–29 12% × 52M = 6.2M; 30–49 24% × 89M = 21.4M; 50–64 33% × 62M = 20.5M; 65+ 12% × 68M = 8.2M; total ≈ 56.2M ≈ 20.7%. Income thirds (23.5/21/17.5) average 20.7. The bottom third rose most, by 7.2 pts, through $49 generic semaglutide at retail and ≈1.4M users of the federally funded community-health-centre programme. The gradient now sits in what people are on and with what monitoring, more than in whether they are on at all. The 65+ band rose 3.5 pts because generic semaglutide reached Part D generic tiers. DEXA waits and the new eye warning slowed it. Off-drug populations: ≈29M ex-users, mostly gated-plan drop-outs, DEXA- or eye-advised pauses, and GI quitters. ≈186M never-users are now concentrated among the under-30s, people who refuse on principle (the backlash coalition, roughly 8–10% of adults by survey), and the rural uninsured above the subsidy's 200%-FPL line who live far from a health centre. Pediatric: ~0.8% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 580k, mostly adolescents 12+ on generic semaglutide, some bought cash by parents. About one US child in five now lives with a parent who is currently on the drug. Adolescent bone-accrual interim data are still unpublished.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: ≈14% of fills ≈ 7.9M users (7.3M aged 65+ plus ≈0.6M disabled under-65). The Bridge successor continues for ≈2.4M obesity users, now with a generic tier. Bridge spend 2032: 1.3M generic × $48 net × 12 ≈ $0.75B, plus 1.1M brand (mostly tirzepatide) × $199 × 12 ≈ $2.63B, ≈ $3.4B in total, down from $4.3B in 2030. Medicaid: ≈10% of fills ≈ 5.6M users. 3.6M generic × $45 × 12 ≈ $1.94B plus 2.0M brand × $199 × 12 ≈ $4.78B gives ≈ $6.7B gross federal+state before rebates, down from $8.4B while users rose 60%. Community Metabolic Health Initiative (HRSA, FY2032 omnibus): free generic semaglutide at federally qualified health centres for uninsured or underinsured adults ≤200% FPL who meet BMI criteria. ≈1.4M enrolled by Dec 2032 × $42 net × 12 ≈ $0.71B for drug, plus ≈$0.35B for visits, weigh-ins and eye/fall screening, ≈ $1.06B against a $1.1B appropriation. The Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 80+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month, and Indian generic tirzepatide is launching in 2032 where patents allow. China: generic semaglutide is widespread, and Chinese tirzepatide and retatrutide-analogue API supplies the research-peptide gray trade. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 40–70. Brazil, Mexico and Turkey have generics. Generic oral semaglutide is sold in most markets outside the US and EU. EU semaglutide generics are expected 2031–33, country by country.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Generic collapse, limited to semaglutide. After patent settlements, five ANDA holders and Novo's authorised generic launched injectable semaglutide in Jan 2032. By Q3, cash prices are $39 (online discount pharmacies), $49–59 (big-box and grocery pharmacies) and $69 (mainstream chains). Branded Wegovy is still listed but has a single-digit share of new semaglutide starts. Oral semaglutide (formulation patents) and Foundayo stay branded at $149–199. Tirzepatide is patent-protected to ~2036, and Lilly answered with $149 starting and $199–249 maintenance on the federal direct portal. Retatrutide is $399 direct, list $1,499. Payer mix of ≈56.2M users: commercial 44% (24.7M), Medicare 14% (7.9M), Medicaid 10% (5.6M), HRSA free provision 2.5% (1.4M), cash/direct 26% (14.6M), imported/counterfeit 3.5% (2.0M) = 100%. Coverage is structurally unchanged. Commercial share drifted down from 47% only because cash generic grew faster. About 70% of covering employers still gate (≥80% PDC, verified weigh-ins, ≥5% at 6 months), now with generic-semaglutide step therapy before tirzepatide. A minority of small employers dropped the benefit, citing $49 cash. Imports fell from ≈3.1M to ≈2.0M users as the price reason disappeared for semaglutide. What remains is mostly gray tirzepatide and 'research' retatrutide vials. Access is now a question of income floor and monitoring. The molecule costs about what a phone bill does. DEXA, eye exams, coaching and the branded dual and triple agonists do not.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic incl. 7.2 mg; US generic semaglutide from Jan 2032)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus; branded in US)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm', 'focus' and 'craving freedom' subscriptions, now mostly low-dose generic injectable semaglutide at $49–69 a month plus a telehealth fee; ≈3.2M subscribers, many without obesity
smoking and vaping cessation (no resubmission yet; widely prescribed off-label)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices, now built around retatrutide or tirzepatide plus DEXA, eye exams and strength coaching
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class and no new indication reached the US market this step. The drivers are honoured with what the approval rules allow. MariTide (filed Apr 2030) received a CRL in Apr 2031 asking for prospective ophthalmic monitoring data in light of the NAION signal, plus 72-week DEXA. Amgen resubmitted in Jun 2032, with a decision expected mid-2033. Amycretin received a CRL in May 2031 over lean-mass data. EMA approved it in Sep 2032 and it is launching in Germany and the Nordics, not the US. Survodutide's resubmission is under review, with action expected 2033. The semaglutide smoking-cessation trial with SHAPS endpoints is enrolling and not expected to read out before 2033. Bimagrumab combinations are still in phase 3. The only US changes are generic semaglutide (Jan 2032) and the NAION class warning on every label, generics included. Incretin market ≈$100–105B in 2032, down from $118B: US semaglutide revenue collapses to generic economics, while tirzepatide and retatrutide volumes grow at falling net prices. Bone agents remain routine co-prescriptions.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common class effect and the leading cause of voluntary discontinuation. Cheap generics bring more self-paced escalation without follow-up visits.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained; identical on generic labels.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss. Retatrutide growth in the top income third keeps case counts rising.
Still no causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Counterfeit confounding is shrinking for semaglutide but persists for gray tirzepatide.

Now income-patterned. A CDC body-composition brief (2032) finds that among users over 50, lean mass accounts for ~38% of weight lost in the bottom income third versus ~24% in the top third, a gap tracking resistance training and protein intake. Generic users at retail mostly have no baseline scan.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 2028 class label and 2029 joint guidance retained. The HRSA programme funds fall-risk screening but not DEXA. No new statute.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: With ≈3.6M 65+ users on >2 years, a ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × 0.35 excess ≈ 7,600 excess hip fractures a year, up from ≈5,000, against ~300,000 US total. The signal in cycling postmenopausal women 50–64 is replicated. DEXA waits in some regions are 10–14 weeks. Mobile DEXA is sold as a premium-gym perk.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling retained; FDA bone endpoints required in all new obesity filings (cited in the MariTide and amycretin CRLs). DOJ civil case against Novo unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Moved from 'very rare' to a class warning. An FDA Sentinel analysis (≈2.3M users) and a pooled Nordic–UK cohort find HR ~2.0–2.4 in users with type 2 diabetes and ~1.4–1.6 without, highest in the first year and in people with crowded optic discs. Absolute risk stays low: an estimated ~1,500–3,000 excess cases a year across ≈56M US users, mostly permanent partial vision loss in one eye.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Aug 2031 class-wide Warnings and Precautions for all GLP-1-containing products, generics included under label sameness. It covers patient counselling on sudden painless vision loss, stopping the drug and urgent ophthalmology referral, and caution with prior NAION. A baseline eye exam is advised for high-risk patients 'where available' but is not required. The NAION MDL expands, and ophthalmology referral volumes rise.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association in updated reviews.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Final retatrutide postmarketing SHAPS data (2031) confirm the interim picture: ~11–13% of top-dose users cross a clinically meaningful anhedonia threshold versus ~5% of comparators, and the effect is dose-dependent. The study is observational. There is still no systematic measurement among the ≈3.2M low-dose 'calm' subscribers.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No label change. FTC consent order (2032) with one telehealth brand bars 'anxiety treatment' and 'clinically proven focus' claims; 'calm' and 'craving freedom' copy is untouched.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Substantial regain within a year. Involuntary stops from gating continue. Pauses advised for eye problems are a new category, alongside DEXA pauses. Cheap restarts shorten off-periods and increase the number of cycles.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly. Indiana waiver litigation still pending in the Seventh Circuit.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency signals are strongest in older and low-income generic users eating sharply less with no dietitian contact.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance (2029) retained. HRSA programme materials include a protein handout. No FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~7 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of follow-up. Cycling's bone penalty is confirmed in a third cohort. Adolescent bone-accrual interim results are still unpublished while pediatric use rises to ≈580k.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements continue; pediatric bone-accrual studies under way.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Falling for semaglutide as $49 legal generics undercut the mail trade; poison-centre calls involving mail-order semaglutide are down ~35% from 2030. Harms shift to gray tirzepatide and 'research-use' retatrutide vials, which carry endotoxin and mg/unit confusion. No repeat of the 2029 insulin-pen cluster.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts and seizures continue; the 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand; still no prosecution of individuals.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated fall-related ED visits in 65+ long-term users persist and are more pronounced among generic-tier users without strength programmes. The confounding is partly separated in one 2032 analysis, giving HR ~1.2.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening is in the Bridge counselling template and the HRSA visit protocol.

safety_ledger.effect: Generic device and pen-format differences (dose-counting errors on switching)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. Generic semaglutide arrives in several pen designs with different click-counts and dose increments. Pharmacy-level substitution produces scattered overdose-by-confusion GI admissions, and calls to manufacturers' lines spiked in Q1 2032.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA drug-safety communication on pen differences (Mar 2032); pharmacist counselling at first generic fill encouraged, not mandated.

food_and_beverage.state: About one adult in five is on the drug, and the losses now reach the bottom third, the volume core of snacks, sugary drinks and value bakery. US salty-snack volume is down ~4% a year in 2031–32 and carbonated soft drinks ~3%. Dollar-store and discount-grocery shelves add $1 'GLP companion' protein shakes and fortified noodle cups. Premium 'bone-forward' dairy and high-protein lines keep growing in affluent channels. Packaged-food majors cut SKUs and shrink pack sizes. None has exited a core category.

alcohol.state: Fourth straight year of US spirits volume decline. Beer falls fastest among working-class men now on $49 generics. 'Calm' subscriptions keep eroding occasional drinking. On-premise 'one good drink' and non-alcoholic formats hold. Tobacco firms report quit rates above trend.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat and spend per cover is down further. Value-volume chains in lower-income markets now feel what suburban chains felt in 2028. Half portions and gram-priced bowls are universal. The 'no-gram' independents in Atlanta, Memphis and Houston are still full. Fast-casual chains test 'protein plates' at value price points aimed at generic users.

apparel.state: Size churn continues, and cut now carries class. Premium brands sell 'structured' lines tailored for resistance-trained shoulders at ~3× core prices. Mass retailers sell drapey, sleeve-forward cuts that hide thin arms. Plus-size specialists hold their audience among people off by conviction.

fitness.state: Split market. Premium 'body-composition' studios bundle quarterly DEXA, coached lifting and eye/bone referral coordination at $300–500/month, and they are growing fast in Austin, Scottsdale and north Atlanta suburbs. Budget gyms grow members but not coaching. Medicare Advantage strength benefits continue. The HRSA programme's 'move' component is a handout and a resistance band.

insurance.state: Structure unchanged. Employers gate as before but now step members through generic semaglutide before tirzepatide. Net GLP-1 spend per covered member fell ~40%, and pharmacy trend eased to ~+3%. Employer coverage edged up to 64% while some small firms dropped the benefit, citing $49 cash. Bone, eye-referral and fracture claims now appear as separate lines in GLP-1 cost models.

pharma.state: Dollar value is falling. US semaglutide revenue moved to generic economics within two quarters. Novo is shrunken, living on oral semaglutide, ex-US CagriSema and an EU amycretin launch. Lilly's tirzepatide and retatrutide grow in volume at lower net prices and dominate the premium tier. Generic makers (Viatris/Biocon, Teva, Sandoz, Dr. Reddy's and others) compete on pen supply. Ophthalmic-imaging and DEXA suppliers are winners.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness is cheap now, so it no longer signals much on its own. Shape and texture carry the signal. A 'dense' look of lean, muscled, upright build with good skin means money: tirzepatide or retatrutide, a coach, quarterly DEXA. 'Generic thin' looks different: soft, narrow-shouldered, thin-armed, sometimes with loose skin at the jaw. It reads as $49 from the grocery pharmacy and no follow-up. A large body reads either as principled (off by conviction) or as rural and uninsured above the subsidy line.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The gradient is in quality and texture, not in whether people are on the drug: top 23.5% vs bottom 17.5% on the drug. In Houston the divide runs almost by zip code. Memorial and River Oaks clients book DEXA-and-barbell studios, while Pasadena and Gulfton residents fill generics at grocery counters and get screened, if at all, at a health centre. Skin-tightening and 'arm reconstruction' clinics advertise in the first group's neighbourhoods. Shapewear and sleeves sell in the second.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are small and protein-first everywhere, and that is no longer a marker of wealth. Wealthier tables show off protein quality and timing: grass-fed, 40 g per plate. Working-class tables eat less of the same food plus a shake. 'Full-table' Sunday dinners, church potlucks and 'no-gram' restaurants remain heritage rituals for the off-by-conviction.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles still state on/off. Upper-income apps add 'body comp verified' badges tied to DEXA reports, which critics call a credit score for flesh. 'Unmedicated' remains an identity filter in backlash communities. Advice columns move on from 'my partner is calm and boring' to 'my partner says I look generic'.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is medicalised, cheap to suppress, and politicised. With the drug free at health centres, the backlash coalition reframes refusal: the religious strand in the Tulsa–Dallas corridor calls free provision 'the government's appetite pill', and Atlanta's body-sovereignty collectives argue that the subsidy treats the poor body as a public-health problem to be quieted rather than fed well. Supplement sellers pivot to 'natural muscle' products aimed at generic users.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Final retatrutide SHAPS data: ~11–13% of top-dose users show clinically meaningful anhedonia versus ~5% of comparators, dose-dependent and observational. Low-dose 'calm' subscriptions grew from ~1.5–2M to ≈3.2M once generic semaglutide let brands sell a $59–79/month bundle of drug plus app. All of these subscribers sit inside the 14.6M cash/direct users, and roughly 40% have a BMI under 27. No independent measurement of mood effects in this group exists.
interior_life.framing: A feature, and cheaper. 'Quiet', 'Even' and 'Unhooked' now ship low-dose generic pens at about the price of a streaming bundle, with copy about calm, focus and freedom from 'noise'. Clinicians say 'dose-dependent reward modulation'. Users who dislike it call it 'the grey', and the FTC's 2032 consent order polices only claims about anxiety treatment and proven focus.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Tech and finance firms still reimburse 'focus' subscriptions from lifestyle accounts, and some call-centre and logistics employers now offer them as an EAP option at $0. Gated coverage still ties adherence to employment-linked insurance. Sales, hospitality and creative workers keep doing dose-holidays before pitches and peak shifts. Some managers in fleet operations prefer calm-subscribed dispatchers and say so off the record.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Written unmedicated' remains a selling point in Nashville songwriting rooms and on comedy tours. A cheaper variant has spread: amateur and church musicians in the South advertise 'no-grey' worship sets. Subscribers keep chasing intensity through ghost-pepper challenges, loud venues and extreme sports. Fans now argue about whether a star's flatter record is 'the grey' or just the premium regimen's polish.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen for dose, product and subscription. Dose-holiday weekends are common. Couples split by product tier, one on a coached tirzepatide plan and one on a generic or calm subscription, describe a mismatch both in bodies and in affect. Backlash groups keep framing the drugs as a threat to marriage and fertility.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: 2032 is an election year, and free provision is on the stump. Its supporters frame it as 'a real pen free beats a fake pen for $20' after the counterfeit deaths, and its opponents in the backlash coalition and among fiscal hawks frame it as pacification or waste. Consultants test 'calm voter' messages privately. There is still no measured turnout or temperament effect, only speculation about how subscriber-heavy suburbs will vote.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding on new entrants (CRLs for MariTide and amycretin) and has moved NAION to a class warning. It approved generic semaglutide ANDAs under settled patent terms and issued a pen-difference safety communication. Enforcement on imports stays selective. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand. The FTC acts on claims only.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Subsidy, no mandate. The FY2032 omnibus (Mar 2032) funds the HRSA Community Metabolic Health Initiative at $1.1B to provide free generic semaglutide, quarterly visits and fall/eye screening at federally qualified health centres for uninsured or underinsured adults ≤200% FPL who meet BMI criteria. ≈1.4M were enrolled by December. The programme has no response threshold and does not fund DEXA. Medicare and Medicaid add generic tiers within existing benefits. The federal direct portal carries branded tirzepatide at $149–249.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in structure. The Indiana and Arkansas waivers (≥80% PDC, quarterly verified weigh-ins, two misses = 12 months off) continue. ~70% of covering employers gate through PBMs with the ≥5% response threshold. BMI-linked surcharges up to 30% of premium remain. Weigh-in kiosks in pharmacy chains also serve HRSA sites. The new NAION stopping advice creates a second kind of medically advised gap that gating rules do not recognise.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still makes incretins a de facto requirement for some drivers. Because of the NAION warning, some fleets now add a vision re-check for drivers on GLP-1s, and FMCSA medical examiners received guidance to ask. Army accession policy on GLP-1 use is unchanged and contested.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Domestic generics depend on Indian and some Chinese API and on contract fill-finish capacity. Section 232 tariffs remain, and 'secure peptide supply' bills are introduced but not passed. With semaglutide imports collapsing, India–US talks shift to tirzepatide patent pressure. China's role moves to gray tirzepatide and retatrutide-analogue API.

events.event: FDA rejects Amgen's monthly MariTide, asking for prospective eye-exam data and 72-week body-composition results; a month later it sends Novo's amycretin back over lean-mass loss, leaving no new incretin class on track for the US before 2033

FDA adds a class-wide warning for sudden optic-nerve vision loss (NAION) to every GLP-1-containing drug after a Sentinel analysis of 2.3 million users finds risk roughly doubled in people with diabetes; patients are told to stop and seek urgent eye care if vision fails

Generic semaglutide launches in the US under patent settlements that let five manufacturers and Novo's own authorised generic enter on the same day; by summer, grocery and discount pharmacies sell a month's pens for $39–69 cash

Spending bill funds a $1.1 billion federal programme giving free generic semaglutide through community health centres to low-income uninsured adults with obesity, backed by lawmakers in both parties who cite the 2029 counterfeit-pen deaths; 1.4 million enrol by December

'Quiet' relaunches on low-dose generic semaglutide at $59 a month and passes 1 million subscribers; the same month the FTC signs a consent order with a rival barring 'anxiety treatment' claims but leaving 'calm' and 'craving freedom' copy intact

CDC body-composition brief finds lower-income GLP-1 users over 50 lose far more muscle per pound than higher-income users; the same week a national apparel chain launches a premium 'Structured' line cut for lifted shoulders at triple its usual prices

open_tensions: The molecule is free or $49, but doing it right is not. DEXA, eye exams, coaching and the branded dual and triple agonists cost $300–500 a month, and the subsidy funds the drug but not the scan. Lean-mass and fracture burdens are moving down the income ladder while body shape becomes a readable class marker.

Gating still rewards continuous use and steady loss, while two kinds of medically advised stop now exist: DEXA-driven bone pauses and NAION-warning eye stops. Either can trip an adherence rule and cost a worker or a waiver enrollee coverage for a year.

Calm subscriptions at $59 reach ≈3.2M people, many without obesity, some paid for by employers. The only rigorous data describe reward blunting as a dose-dependent harm, and regulators police the advertising copy, not the product.

The HRSA programme depends on an annual appropriation in an election year that the backlash coalition and fiscal hawks both target, while tirzepatide's patents run to ~2036 and the gray market has moved to counterfeit tirzepatide and 'research' retatrutide.
still_true: The Indiana and Arkansas Medicaid 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins; two misses end coverage for 12 months, and the disability-rights litigation is still unresolved in the Seventh Circuit.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The 503B exclusion and the 503A injunction on compounded incretins both still stand.
About 70% of covering employers still use outcome-gated PBM designs with a ≥5%-at-six-months response threshold, and BMI-linked wellness surcharges up to the 30%-of-premium ceiling remain legal.
Retatrutide's list price is still $1,499 a month, with a $399 direct price, and it remains branded-only from Lilly.

prose.headline: Forty-Nine Dollars to Be Thin, Four Hundred to Look Rich: How America's Cheapest Drug Made Bodies Readable
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 about one American adult in five is on an incretin drug, and the most important fact about the drug is that it has become ordinary. In January, under patent settlements negotiated long before, five manufacturers and Novo's own authorised-generic arm launched semaglutide on the same morning. By summer a month of pens costs thirty-nine dollars online, forty-nine at a grocery pharmacy, sixty-nine at a mainstream chain. Branded Wegovy still has a list price, and hardly anyone starts on it now.

Nothing else about who pays changed. Employers still gate their coverage through the same pharmacy-benefit managers, with the same verified scales and the same five-percent threshold, now with a rule that members try generic semaglutide before tirzepatide. Medicare and Medicaid added generic tiers and spend less on more people. The one new thing is public. In March, a spending bill that otherwise pleased nobody funded free generic semaglutide at community health centres for low-income uninsured adults, on the argument that a real pen given away beats a fake pen bought for twenty dollars. About 1.4 million people have enrolled. The programme pays for the drug, a quarterly visit, a fall screen and an eye question. It does not pay for a bone scan.

That gap is where the country now sorts itself. When thinness cost a thousand dollars a month, it was the signal. Now that it costs a phone bill, the signal is texture. In north Houston, Scottsdale and the suburbs above Atlanta, the look is dense: lifted shoulders, upright posture, quarterly DEXA reports, tirzepatide or retatrutide from Lilly's portal, and a coach who books the eye referral. In Pasadena, Texas, or south Memphis, the look is generic thin: narrow, soft, thin in the arm, a little loose at the jaw. A September federal brief put a number on it. Lower-income users over fifty lose far more muscle per pound than wealthier ones. The same week, an apparel chain launched a line cut for lifted shoulders at triple its usual price. Neither surprised anyone.

The eyes are the new caution. In August 2031 the FDA moved optic-nerve stroke from a footnote to a class warning on every GLP-1 label, generics included, after a large federal analysis found the risk roughly doubled in people with diabetes. The absolute numbers are small, perhaps a few thousand excess cases a year among fifty-six million users, and almost all of them mean partial and permanent loss of sight in one eye. Patients are told to stop and seek urgent care if vision fails. Gated plans do not distinguish that stop from any other missed fill. The bones keep their slow arithmetic too, at roughly seventy-six hundred extra hip fractures a year.

The quieting effect is cheaper as well. 'Quiet' and its rivals now ship low-dose generic pens for about sixty dollars a month to some three million subscribers, many of them never heavy, some reimbursed by employers as a focus perk. The FTC struck the word 'anxiety' from one brand's copy and left 'calm' alone. The only rigorous data, from retatrutide, still say that at high doses roughly one user in eight loses meaningful pleasure.

The backlash has not shrunk, but its target has moved from cost to the subsidy. Pentecostal pulpits from Tulsa to Dallas call it the government's appetite pill. Atlanta's body-sovereignty collectives say it quiets poor bodies instead of feeding them. It is an election year, and both parties' candidates are courting both groups. Snack and beer volumes fall fastest now in discount aisles. Seen from outside, it looks like public health working, and in part it is.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Dwayne Pruitt clocks out of the distribution centre in Southaven at 2:40 and drives up Elvis Presley Boulevard to the health centre, where the parking lot has a new banner with a smiling woman in scrubs and the words FREE. REAL. MONITORED.

The kiosk takes his thumb and his weight: 241, down from 268. The nurse asks the questions off a laminated card. Any falls. Any sudden change in your vision, either eye, even for a minute. He says no, then admits the left one was blurry Sunday morning before church. She shines a light in it for a long time and writes something. She says the eye clinic at the Med has a six-week wait. She says if it happens again he should stop the pens and go to the ER, and not to wait for her to call.

He gets two boxes, a resistance band in a plastic sleeve, and a sheet about protein with a cartoon egg on it.

At home Keisha has the oven on. She is not on it and won't be. She calls it the government's pill, but not in a mean way. She makes him a plate that is half chicken and pushes the cornbread toward their son.

After dinner he stands at the bathroom mirror and lifts his arm. It hangs thinner than he expected. His supervisor's arms don't do that. His supervisor pays somebody in Germantown to scan him.

He covers one eye, then the other, reading the shampoo bottle.

It's Thursday, his shot night. He holds the pen for a while and then clicks it.
